notes: Caches grow beyond four boxes. Add one or ten at a time, or upgrade the interfaces from 100G to 400G and 1.6T. Boxes share a scalable pool instead of creating thousands of routing exits. Router ports, service fees and metered electricity still matter; overflow uses peering or transit.

Full circuits pause the game at 100% load, with an Inspect shortcut. Resume without repeated interruptions: a circuit re-arms only below 90% load. Disable this independently of customer warnings in Settings.

Customers can request bandwidth expansions with 30 days' notice. Accept to schedule the extra capacity and revenue, or keep the current contract. Nothing changes automatically; accepted expansions get 15 days of grace.
Tablet double taps no longer trigger default page zoom. Pinch zoom still works, lifting one finger resumes panning, and the menu can reset the map.

Ten new hubs fill gaps: Vancouver, Winnipeg, Casablanca, Dakar, Accra, Luanda, Dar es Salaam, Tashkent, Almaty and Hanoi. They include transit, local peering, fabric access and three game-world coastal cable systems.

Endgame room: a 204.8T modular router, up to 64 routers and LAG members, 256 racks per POP, 1.6T fabrics and virtual circuits, and 409.6T own IXs. Parallel waves and fiber remain available for further backbone growth.
Fixed North American power tariffs using the wrong region key, invalid NNI and circuit data breaking imported saves, and phantom router capacity when no router remained available.
